Practice: forming and using your own Yinyang

Forming your own Yinyang connects a philosophy you can express, an understanding of the actual participants, and an environment through which they can work. The point is a practice that enters life: what you can understand, create, judge, and do with a capable model counterpart. The author's Stealing fire develops this as cultivation through borrowed generative capacity. Your own philosophy can adopt, combine, challenge, and rewrite existing thought into a direction you choose.

Philosophy and models develop together

Full formation includes writing your own philosophy. It can begin with a question, image, way of working, or something understood through life. Literature, humanities, engineering philosophy, Western philosophy, philosophy of science, logic, and aesthetics can each contribute. No academic curriculum or completed theory is required before useful work begins.

Philosophy articulates concepts, reasons, values, and possibilities. Personal material grounds their application to an actual person, counterpart, and relationship. Either can revise the other. A chosen direction differs from an explanation of experience; a desired model contribution differs from demonstrated capability. Philosophy and models develops these connections and leads to the six writing files.

Starting conditions and order vary. You may already have philosophical expression, a history of personal inquiry, or a working environment. Develop the missing connections from there. A tool or a work can disclose a relation that later acquires philosophical expression. Forming one's own philosophy remains part of fully forming one's own Yinyang; borrowing an idea for another task need not undertake that whole practice.

Six files give the practice a usable form

Five accounts articulate the adopted orientation, actual person, model counterpart, relationship, and environment. The sixth file guides their revision and is itself revised through use. Their writing guidance belongs with those six objects: the five account guides and revision. Environmental realization belongs in the environment writing; continuing change belongs in the sixth file.

The five actual accounts remain private, with evidence at its appropriate owners; public distribution supplies guidance, not a copied portrait. Prompts, Skills, tools, and interfaces give understood relations working consequences. Those consequences can correct the accounts and philosophy. Completed output, collaborative fit, and developing personal capacity call for evidence at their respective scales.

Using Yinyang

People and models can read and use these materials together: develop an argument, compare an account with experience, inspect an arrangement, or make an authorized change. Different writing forms serve different contributions without reserving philosophy for humans or practical understanding for models.

Using Yinyang explains how the current six files cooperate in ordinary work. The package guide explains their common and private paths and shared updates. These are connected entrances, not a sequence to repeat for every task. The example and commons essay invites selective adoption, combination, and independent authorship.
